title: Rule complexity does not determine behavioral complexity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rule complexity does not determine behavioral complexity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: There is no direct correspondence between the complexity of a system's underlying rules and the complexity of its behavior: some of the simplest rules yield highly complex behavior, fairly complicated rules often yield simple behavior, and rules differing at a single position can behave very differently.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Traditional intuition might have made one assume that there must be a direct correspondence between the complexity of observed behavior and the complexity of underlying rules. But one of the central discoveries of this book is that in fact there is not.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “Origins of Simple Behavior” (from p. 351), p. 351. Scope: simple programs such as cellular automata, and by extension natural systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-20: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: For specified simple-program families the rules and outputs are fully available and standard computations can test direct correspondence. The claim only requires demonstrating lack of a universal direct mapping, for which clear counterexamples are decisive. Multiple complexity metrics should be used to ensure the result is not an artifact of one encoding.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Choose explicit rule-description and spacetime-behavior complexity measures, enumerate bounded simple-program families, and estimate their association while examining minimally differing rule pairs. Counterexamples in both directions and weak correspondence would support the claim; a robust monotone mapping would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Complexity has several inequivalent measures.

The extension from formal programs to natural systems is not resolved by enumeration.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a statement about simple programs, and the elementary cellular automata are a finite public object. Recomputing the Gray-code sequence of neighboring rules and scoring their output takes days with standard tools. A direct correspondence would show up as a strong correlation; its absence is a decisive result for the stated scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate small cellular-automaton rule spaces, measure rule-table complexity against a behavioral-complexity statistic such as spacetime compressibility or Wolfram class, and compare rules that differ by one table entry. A weak or absent correlation, with adjacent rules in different classes, would support the claim; a tight monotone relation between rule complexity and behavioral complexity would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Behavioral complexity has several inequivalent measures, though the qualitative mismatch is stable across the usual ones.

fields.label: Dimension scores

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Across exhaustively enumerated families of simple programs, measures of the complexity of a rule's definition are at most weakly rank-correlated with measures of the complexity of the behaviour it produces; some rules of minimal definitional complexity produce behaviour in the top quartile of behavioural complexity, some rules of maximal definitional complexity produce behaviour in the bottom quartile, and a non-negligible fraction of rules that differ in a single table entry differ greatly in behavioural complexity.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py enumerates the 256 elementary rules and the 2187 three-colour totalistic codes, computes the rule-complexity measures (ANF monomial count by Moebius transform; minimal two-input gate count by breadth-first search over all 3-input truth tables with free negation; table entropy; non-default entries) and runs each rule from a random initial condition (width 300, periodic, seed 20260720, 200-step transient, 400 recorded steps) and from a single seed (400 steps, width 801), compressing each space-time diagram with lzma preset 9. Spearman correlations were computed for the 8 (rule measure, behaviour measure) pairs, quartile counterexamples were listed, and the 1024 Hamming-distance-1 pairs of elementary rules were compared on the random-IC compressed size. Run time about 4 minutes.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Families: (F1) the 256 elementary cellular automata; (F2) the 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic cellular automata (Wolfram codes 0..2186). Rule-complexity measures: F1: (a) number of monomials in the algebraic normal form over GF(2), (b) minimal number of two-input gates (AND, OR, XOR, with negation free) computing the rule, found by breadth-first search over truth tables; F2: (c) Shannon entropy in bits of the 7-entry code table, (d) number of table entries that differ from the table's most frequent value. Behaviour-complexity measures: (e) lzma-compressed size (preset 9) of the space-time diagram, one byte per cell, from a random initial condition (width 300, periodic boundary, numpy seed 20260720, steps 200..600 after a 200-step transient); (f) the same for the single-seed pattern (one black / one gray cell, 400 steps, width 801, zero boundary). Statistics: Spearman rank correlation rho for each (rule measure, behaviour measure) pair within each family (8 pairs). 'supports' if max over the 8 pairs of rho <= 0.30, and in each family at least one rule at the minimum value of each rule measure has behaviour measure (e) in the top quartile of its family while at least one rule at the maximum value has (e) in the bottom quartile, and at least 5 % of F1 Hamming-distance-1 rule pairs (1024 pairs) differ in (e) by more than half of the family's range of (e).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if any of the 8 Spearman correlations is >= 0.60 (a direct, monotone correspondence between rule complexity and behaviour complexity) or if in either family no rule at minimal rule complexity reaches the top quartile of behaviour complexity. Otherwise (e.g. 0.30 < max rho < 0.60, or the Hamming-neighbour fraction below 5 %) -> 'mixed'.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: Spearman rho between rule complexity and lzma size of the space-time diagram; fraction of 1024 Hamming-1 ECA pairs whose random-IC lzma sizes differ by more than half the family range

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: one random initial condition per rule; lzma sizes in bytes (ECA random-IC range 152..17028)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: 'Complexity of underlying rules' is operationalised by syntactic measures of the rule table (ANF size and minimal circuit size for Boolean rules; entropy and non-default entries for totalistic codes), and 'complexity of behaviour' by lossless compressibility of the space-time diagram, which treats both random-looking and structured-but-irregular behaviour as complex (Wolfram's usage also counts class 3 randomness as complex). 'No direct correspondence' is read as the absence of a strong monotone association (rho < 0.3 weak, rho >= 0.6 strong) plus the existence of the counterexamples Wolfram describes. The extension 'and by extension natural systems' is not tested. All patterns are generated by analysis.py; there is no external download.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Elementary cellular automata (256 rules, Wolfram numbering) and three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic cellular automata (2187 codes, Wolfram code numbering: code digit k in base 3 gives the new colour for neighbourhood sum k), generated by analysis.py with the initial conditions, widths, step counts and seed stated in pass_criterion

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The pre-registered decision rule is degenerate and the verdict is therefore recorded as inconclusive rather than as the 'refutes' it literally produces: the rule required a rule 'at the minimum value of each rule measure' to reach the top behavioural quartile, but the minimum of every measure is attained only by constant rules (rule 0; the three constant totalistic codes; for the gate count, the eight 0-gate projections/negations), which cannot produce complex behaviour under any definition. The condition therefore tests nothing about the claim. This is an error in the pre-registration, discovered only after the run.

Post hoc (not pre-registered): at the lowest non-constant complexity levels there are rules in the top behavioural quartile, as the claim asserts: with 2 ANF monomials rules 60, 90 and 102 (nested), with 1 gate the same rules plus 153, 165, 195, and with 2 gates rules 30 and 45 (random-looking, essentially incompressible: 16952 and 16932 bytes vs a maximum of 17028). At the highest gate count (4) rules 77, 104, 232 and 233 sit in the bottom quartile, and 65 maximum-entropy totalistic codes do likewise. Rules differing in one table entry differ by more than half the behavioural range in 19.2 % of the 1024 pairs (e.g. 14/30, 6/22, 2/18), far above the pre-registered 5 %.

All eight Spearman correlations are positive but weak to moderate (0.13 to 0.41; the four elementary-rule correlations are 0.13 to 0.41 and the four totalistic ones 0.30 to 0.38). None reaches the pre-registered 0.60 'direct correspondence' threshold, but the maximum (0.41, ANF monomials vs single-seed compressibility) exceeds the 0.30 'weak' threshold, so under the pre-registered thresholds with the degenerate clause removed the outcome would have been 'mixed': there is some statistical association between rule and behaviour complexity, but nothing like a monotone correspondence, and the counterexamples Wolfram describes exist.

Compressibility of a random-initial-condition diagram is a poor proxy for behavioural complexity for shift-like class 2 rules (e.g. rule 15 transports the random input and so compresses badly) and for additive rules; the single-seed measure corrects this for those cases but conflates nested with random behaviour less well. Only one random initial condition per rule was used. The 'natural systems' extension of the claim was not tested.
